title: Bridge a Calendar without touching it

blocks.text: An old library hands you `java.util.Calendar` objects and wants them back. A `Calendar` is mutable, and the library keeps using the ones it gave you.

items: `toZoned(Calendar calendar)`: the same moment as a `ZonedDateTime` in the calendar's **own time zone**. Most calendars are `GregorianCalendar`s, but **any** `Calendar` must convert, such as the Japanese imperial calendar.
`plusOneDay(Calendar calendar)`: a new `Calendar`, one calendar day later at the **same wall-clock time** in the same zone. The caller's calendar is **never changed**.

cases.says: A UTC GregorianCalendar converts to the same moment and local time, and a day later is 24 hours on.
A New York calendar converts to a ZonedDateTime in America/New_York at its local time.
A Japanese imperial calendar converts through its instant and its time zone.
After plusOneDay the caller's Calendar still holds its original time, and a different object is returned.
Noon in New York the day before the clocks spring forward becomes noon the next day, 23 hours later.

concepts: GregorianCalendar.toZonedDateTime() and GregorianCalendar.from(ZonedDateTime) bridge Calendar and ZonedDateTime, keeping the calendar's zone.
A Calendar that is not a GregorianCalendar converts through toInstant() and getTimeZone().toZoneId().
TimeZone.toZoneId() and TimeZone.getTimeZone(ZoneId) convert between the legacy and the modern zone types.
